description: Issue #839: with THREE declarations of `step`, the first finding is at the SECOND (line 4) — the first collision in source order — and its `params.original_span` names line 1. Issue #815 strengthened this fixture without an edit to its data beyond the added finding: the check now reports EVERY copy, so the third declaration (line 7) is reported too, and its `original_span` also names line 1. That second finding is the first-vs-most-recent property this fixture previously disclaimed — at run time alone the two were indistinguishable, because execution halted at the first duplicate and the map only ever held first declarations. It is still pinned independently at check stage by `core-language/check/duplicate-definition-not-profile-gated` and `data/check/duplicate-definition-across-declaration-slots`, each of which declares one name three times so that BOTH later findings name the first declaration rather than the one before them. The three bodies print different values so the fixture also stays sensitive to any override rule sneaking back in. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
